plants.name: Tulipa gesneriana
plants.description: A bulbous perennial with cup-shaped flowers on sturdy stems above broad, blue-green leaves. Thousands of cultivars exist, ranging from simple single blooms to frilly parrot and double forms. April 24 is near peak bloom in the Netherlands and much of northern Europe and the northeastern United States.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid to late spring (April to May in the Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Cultivated worldwide; especially famous in the Netherlands, Northern Europe, and North America; native to Central Asia
plants.funFact: During the Dutch 'Tulip Mania' of the 1630s, a single rare bulb could sell for more than the price of a luxurious canal house in Amsterdam.

plants.name: Wisteria sinensis
plants.description: A vigorous woody climbing vine producing dramatic hanging clusters (racemes) of fragrant, pea-like flowers that open before or as the leaves emerge. It can climb pergolas, walls, and trees, and its blooms create spectacular cascading curtains of color.
plants.location: Native to China; widely cultivated in Europe, Japan, and the United States
plants.funFact: Wisteria vines can live for over a hundred years, and the famous Chinese wisteria in Sierra Madre, California, covers nearly an acre and weighs hundreds of tons.

plants.name: Hyacinthoides non-scripta
plants.description: A bulbous woodland perennial forming dense carpets under deciduous trees. Its nodding, bell-shaped, sweetly scented flowers droop on one side of an arching stem. Late April is the peak of bluebell season in British woodlands.
plants.location: Native to Western Europe, especially the British Isles; ancient woodlands
plants.funFact: About half of the world's bluebells grow in the UK, and it is illegal to collect wild bluebell bulbs there under wildlife protection law.

plants.name: Jacaranda mimosifolia
plants.description: A tall, graceful, semi-deciduous tree with fern-like leaves that bursts into masses of trumpet-shaped lilac-blue flowers. In the Southern Hemisphere, some trees may bloom sporadically in autumn, while in warm northern subtropical regions such as parts of Mexico, Florida, and southern Asia, spring blooming begins around this time.
plants.bloomingSeason: Spring to early summer in the Northern Hemisphere subtropics (April to June); October to December in the Southern Hemisphere
plants.location: Native to South America (Argentina, Bolivia); planted in Mexico, Florida, South Africa, Australia, and the Mediterranean
plants.funFact: In Pretoria, South Africa, tens of thousands of jacarandas earned it the nickname 'Jacaranda City', and fallen blossoms form purple carpets on the streets.
